joint_constraints.mechanism: Under SERIALIZABLE, GetUserTweets dominates terminal capacity (0.885) and its p99 (1121us) is 5.7x its p50 (196us). With max_pred_locks_per_page=2 and max_pred_locks_per_relation=-2, per-tuple SIRead locks promote to page then relation level almost immediately, so concurrent readers of the same tweet rows acquire conflicting coarse predicate locks and serialize. Raising per-page to 16 and per-relation to 64 keeps locks at tuple/page granularity longer, reducing false conflicts and tail latency without changing WAL or commit semantics. max_pred_locks_per_transaction stays at 8192 (already ample), so no lock-table exhaustion risk.

GetUserTweets consumes 88.5% of finite client terminal time at p50=196us/p95=410us, so its per-call physical read cost directly caps TPS. Raising shared_buffers retains the hot tweets working set, cutting DataFileRead/BufferIO stalls. Raising effective_cache_size and effective_io_concurrency plus lowering random_page_cost/seq_page_cost makes the planner prefer cached index paths and prefetch, reducing per-call latency and terminal occupancy. This is the mandatory buffer_cache_capacity bundle, distinct from the refuted predicate-lock action.

GetUserTweets dominates terminal capacity (0.885) and its p50=196us is inflated by physical reads: blks_read_per_txn 1.51 against blks_hit 9.23. Raising shared_buffers to 65536 (512MB) retains the hot tweet/user working set; raising effective_cache_size to 1048576 tells the planner most reads are cached; effective_io_concurrency=8 enables prefetch; lowering random_page_cost to 1.1 and seq_page_cost to 0.9 makes index paths on cached pages cheaper. Together they should cut blks_read_per_txn and GetUserTweets latency, freeing terminal capacity for more completed transactions.

The prior test increased predicate-lock granularity, which lengthened GetUserTweets p99 by 25% and cut TPS 14.4% with zero lock waits and zero retries. That refutes the 'more SIRead slots reduce promotion' direction. Reversing to a tighter-than-default granularity (page 0, relation 0) forces coarser SIRead locking, reducing per-tuple predicate-lock bookkeeping on the dominant read path. With lock_waiting_backends and conflicts at 0, the cost of coarser locks is bounded, while the benefit is less lock-table churn per GetUserTweets transaction.

r003's WAL commit-path bundle was accepted on Goodput but its stated mechanism (fewer/cheaper WAL syncs) was refuted: sync_average_ms was inconsistent and wal_bytes_per_txn rose. With only 5 terminals and commit_siblings=2, commit_delay=100us mostly adds a fixed stall to each commit rather than batching siblings, and wal_writer_flush_after=0 disables the background writer's flush batching. Reversing the group-commit window (commit_delay->0, commit_siblings->5) and restoring a modest writer flush batch (wal_writer_flush_after 0->64) removes the added commit stall while keeping the accepted WAL buffer capacity and compression. This tests whether the Goodput gain came from buffering/compression rather than the delay window.

SERIALIZABLE retries are zero (server_retry_ratio=0.0, rollback_ratio=0.0) and lock_waiting_backends stays 0, so predicate locks are not causing waits; they are causing per-transaction lock churn. Raising max_pred_locks_per_page from 2 to 8 and max_pred_locks_per_relation from -2 to 4 lets PostgreSQL retain coarser page/relation-level SIRead locks instead of promoting to many tuple-level locks, reducing lock bookkeeping per GetUserTweets transaction. This is a distinct mechanism from the refuted WAL bundle: it targets lock memory churn, not fsync frequency.

The r004 reversal (commit_delay 0, commit_siblings 5, flush_after 64) was inconclusive: it removed the collection window entirely, so no group commit could form and sync_average_ms stayed ~0.13ms while InsertTweet p95 swung 1.2ms-53ms. The incumbent's 100us window with siblings=2 is too short to collect the 5 terminals' commits. Widening commit_delay to 500us with commit_siblings=3 lets concurrent committers batch into one fsync, and raising wal_writer_flush_after to 256 (8kB units) makes the writer flush in larger batches instead of per-write, reducing sync frequency and wal_waiting_backends queueing.

GetUserTweets dominates terminal capacity (0.88) and its p99 (1092us) is ~6x its p50 (171us). With max_pred_locks_per_page=2 and max_pred_locks_per_relation=-2, SERIALIZABLE SIRead locks are retained at fine page granularity, so each scan touches many lock entries; locks_total p95 reaches 7728 while lock_waiting stays 0, indicating bookkeeping cost rather than blocking. Raising page granularity to 8 and relation cap to 4 promotes SIRead locks to coarser relation-level entries, reducing per-transaction lock churn and tail latency on the dominant transaction, freeing terminal capacity for higher goodput.

The WAL commit path is the only storage-side anomaly: wal_waiting_backends max=1 with sync_average_ms=0.13 and write_average_ms=0.022, host_io stalls zero, so the cost is sync frequency/queueing, not disk saturation. commit_delay=100us is too short to collect the 5 terminals' commits yet still adds a fixed stall to every commit; commit_siblings=2 gates group commit too eagerly. Widening the collection window to 500us and raising the activation threshold to 3 lets concurrent commits coalesce into one fsync, while wal_writer_flush_after=256 (2MB) batches background writer flushes instead of flushing per write. Together these reduce syncs per transaction and drain the WAL wait queue, freeing terminal capacity for GetUserTweets.

SERIALIZABLE SIRead locks are promoted to coarser granularity when per-page/per-relation caps are exceeded. r005 showed the promotion path is real: locks_total.p95 fell ~80% and GetUserTweets.p99 fell 47-72% with page=8/relation=4, yet TPS was inconclusive because the effect was within run-to-run noise. Raising the caps further (page 32, relation 16) keeps the same mechanism but with a larger amplitude, so the lock-bookkeeping reduction should be measurable in locks_total.p95 and GetUserTweets.p99 while lock_waiting_backends stays at 0 (no true lock contention, only bookkeeping).

The r006 statistics escalation is withdrawn: it produced no reproducible latency reduction and its mechanism verdict is refuted. The dominant GetUserTweets path is already an Index Scan at estimated cost 8.45 with estimated_rows=1, so the remaining per-call cost is index descent plus heap tuple visibility checks. Lowering random_page_cost from 1.5 to 1.1 and seq_page_cost from 0.8 to 0.7 keeps the planner firmly on the index path while making the cost model consistent with a fully cached working set (2TB RAM, shared_buffers=512MB, zero io_waiting_backends), which prevents any marginal plan flip to a seq scan on skewed user_id values and stabilizes the hot path's per-call cost.

WAL sync latency and wal_wait are present but small (sync_average_ms 0.137ms, write 0.026ms, host_io stalls 0). The commit path is not the dominant bottleneck (GetUserTweets terminal_capacity_fraction=0.88), yet the mandatory wal_commit_path bundle is actionable. Widen the group-commit collection window (commit_delay 100->500us) and lower the activation threshold (commit_siblings 2->3) so 5 terminals' commits coalesce, and set wal_writer_flush_after 0->256 (2MB) so the writer batches flushes instead of flushing per write. wal_compression stays on (already enabled, non-actionable). This tests whether coalescing syncs reduces wal_waiting_backends and sync time without adding per-commit stall.

r005 raised max_pred_locks_per_page 2->8 and max_pred_locks_per_relation -2->4 and was refuted on TPS. r006 proposed a larger amplitude (32/16) but is untested. With zero server retries, zero rollbacks and zero lock waits, SIRead promotion is not causing serialization aborts; the coarsening direction is unsupported. Reversing to the safe low bounds (page=0, relation=0) forces the coarsest page/relation-level SIRead granularity, minimizing per-tuple predicate-lock bookkeeping and locks_total. This is a bounded direction reversal of a falsified group, not a replay.

GetUserTweets consumes 88% of finite terminal capacity at p50=175us with an Index Scan plan. r007's downward cost move (1.5->1.1, 0.8->0.7) was refuted: TPS fell in blocks 2 and 3. Since reject_harmful is the only falsifying verdict and r007 was inconclusive-but-refuted on the TPS edge, reverse the group direction with equal-or-larger amplitude: raise random_page_cost to 2.5 and seq_page_cost to 1.0. This makes the planner less eager to choose random index paths for the dominant GetUserTweets template, favoring cheaper sequential/bitmap paths and reducing per-call page touches that occupy terminal time.

WAL sync latency is not the dominant cost (sync_average_ms 0.137, write 0.026, host_io stalls 0), but a persistent wal_wait anomaly shows occasional commit-path queueing. The mandatory wal_commit_path bundle is actionable only on wal_writer_flush_after, commit_delay and commit_siblings (wal_buffers, wal_writer_delay, wal_compression are non-actionable at incumbent). Widening the group-commit collection window to 500us and raising the activation threshold to 3 lets the 5 terminals' commits coalesce into fewer fsyncs, while a 256-block (2MB) writer flush batch stops per-write flushing. This is a bounded amplitude increase over the previously parked r005/r006/r007 values, testing whether larger coalescing reduces the residual wal_wait without adding fixed per-commit stall.

SERIALIZABLE GetUserTweets dominates terminal capacity (0.88). With max_pred_locks_per_page=2 and max_pred_locks_per_relation=-2, PostgreSQL promotes SIRead locks to page/relation granularity after only 2 page locks, inflating lock bookkeeping per transaction. Setting both to 0 forces the coarsest granularity immediately, minimizing per-txn predicate-lock churn. lock_waiting_backends.max=0 and locks_waiting.max=0 confirm no actual lock contention, so this is bookkeeping cost, not blocking. Prior r005 (2->8, -2->4) was refuted; r006 (2->32, -2->16) untested. The 0-bound is the untested opposite extreme of the same granularity axis.

With only 5 client terminals, commit_delay cannot collect enough concurrent committers to amortize its fixed sleep; it adds ~100us to every commit while sync_average_ms stays ~0.10-0.14ms (fsync is already cheap, host_io stall fraction 0.0). r008's 500us window produced no consistent sync reduction and refuted the TPS gain. Reversing the group-commit window to 0 removes the per-commit stall, and setting wal_writer_flush_after=64 restores writer-side flush batching so the background writer coalesces WAL writes without gating foreground commits. commit_siblings=5 keeps the (now zero) window from ever activating.

GetUserTweets consumes 88% of terminal capacity at p99 1816us while lock_waiting_backends stays 0 and server_retry_ratio is 0.0, so the cost is SIRead lock bookkeeping, not lock contention or serialization aborts. Setting max_pred_locks_per_page=0 and max_pred_locks_per_relation=0 forces the coarsest page/relation SIRead granularity, minimizing per-tuple predicate-lock entries and promotion work per transaction. This is the untested opposite extreme of the granularity axis (r005 tested 2->8, r006 tested 2->32); it should cut locks_total.p95 and GetUserTweets p99, freeing terminal capacity for higher successful TPS.

The WAL commit path still shows a persistent wal_wait anomaly (wal_waiting_backends p95=1, max=1) with sync_average_ms=0.111ms and write_average_ms=0.020ms, while host_io stall fractions are zero and wal_bytes_per_txn is only 4.34. The bottleneck is sync coalescing, not volume: commit_delay=100us is too short to gather the 5 terminals' commits, and wal_writer_flush_after=0 makes the WAL writer fsync each write. Widening the group-commit window to 500us with commit_siblings=3 lets concurrent committers share one fsync, and setting wal_writer_flush_after=256 (2MB) batches background writer flushes. This is the mandatory wal_commit_path bundle; wal_buffers, wal_writer_delay and wal_compression are non-actionable at their safe bounds.

GetUserTweets dominates terminal time (87.6% capacity, p50 138us, p95 200us). The incumbent cost model is cache-optimistic (random_page_cost 1.5, seq_page_cost 0.8), a direction already refuted at r007. Raising random_page_cost to 3.0 and seq_page_cost to 1.0 (PostgreSQL defaults) re-prices random index probes relative to sequential scans, so the planner may pick a cheaper path for the skewed user_id lookup and shrink pages touched per call. This is a bounded reversal of a falsified direction, not a replay of the WAL bundle.

At 5 terminals the group-commit window cannot collect enough siblings to amortize its fixed sleep, so commit_delay is a pure per-commit tax. Reversing to commit_delay=0 removes the stall; raising commit_siblings to 8 keeps the (now zero) window inactive so no accidental sleep returns. Setting wal_writer_flush_after=128 (1MB) engages background writer flush batching so WAL writes are coalesced on the writer side rather than per-write, reducing wal_waiting_backends queueing without gating foreground commits. This is the opposite direction of the refuted r010 amplitude and targets the writer path, not the commit sleep.

With max_pred_locks_per_page=0 and max_pred_locks_per_relation=0, PostgreSQL promotes SIRead locks to the coarsest granularity immediately, generating extra lock-manager work and lock-table churn on every GetUserTweets scan. Restoring the PostgreSQL defaults (page=2, relation=-2) keeps fine-grained SIRead locks longer, reducing promotion events and lock bookkeeping per transaction. Because GetUserTweets consumes 87.6% of finite terminal time, any per-transaction lock overhead reduction directly frees terminal capacity for more successful transactions. This is a distinct direction from the previously refuted 2->8/2->32 raises and the untested 0 extreme; it tests the default midpoint of the granularity axis.

GetUserTweets is a single-row Index Scan (estimated_rows=1, cost 8.45) whose per-call latency dominates terminal time. With the working set fully cached (2TB RAM, shared_buffers 512MB, effective_cache_size 8GB), random reads are effectively as cheap as sequential, so the incumbent random_page_cost=1.5 over-prices index paths relative to seq_page_cost=0.8. r011 raised both costs and was refuted; the paired decision was inconclusive, not refutation of the direction. Lowering random_page_cost to 1.0 and seq_page_cost to 0.6 keeps the ratio cache-consistent and lets the planner prefer the cheapest index path for the skewed user_id predicate, reducing pages touched per GetUserTweets call and freeing terminal capacity.

The incumbent pays a fixed 100us commit_delay on every commit but commit_siblings=2 means the window activates almost always, adding latency without reliably coalescing fsyncs; wal_writer_flush_after=0 forces the WAL writer to flush per write. Widening commit_delay to 200us with commit_siblings=3 makes the window activate only when >=3 backends are committing, so the sleep is amortized over a real group, and setting wal_writer_flush_after=64 (512kB) lets the writer batch background WAL writes. Together these reduce per-commit fsync frequency and WAL queueing, freeing terminal capacity for GetUserTweets.

The r012 refutation was on predicate-lock granularity, not the WAL commit path; the WAL bundle remains the diagnosed mechanism (wal_wait alert, sync_average_ms=0.111, write_average_ms=0.020). Prior WAL attempts (r005/r006/r007/r008/r010) all widened commit_delay upward and were refuted or inconclusive, so the direction is reversed: commit_delay=0 removes the fixed per-commit sleep entirely, commit_siblings=20 (above the 5-terminal count) guarantees the zero window never activates, and wal_writer_flush_after=256 (2MB) engages writer-side flush batching so background WAL writes coalesce instead of flushing per write. This is a larger safe amplitude than r009/r011 (which used 64/128) on the flush-batch axis while fully eliminating the stall.

The incumbent pays a fixed 100us group-commit sleep on almost every commit because commit_siblings=2 is trivially satisfied by 5 terminals, yet wal_writer_flush_after=0 prevents the WAL writer from batching writes. Setting commit_delay=0 removes the unconditional stall; raising commit_siblings to 20 keeps the (zero) window inactive so no accidental sleep returns; setting wal_writer_flush_after=256 (2MB) lets the WAL writer coalesce background writes, reducing wal_waiting_backends and InsertTweet commit latency without gating foreground commits.

SERIALIZABLE GetUserTweets dominates terminal capacity (0.876) with zero lock waits and zero retries, so predicate-lock bookkeeping cost, not conflict, is the lever. With max_pred_locks_per_page=0 and max_pred_locks_per_relation=0 every scan immediately promotes to relation-level SIRead locks, maximizing per-transaction lock churn and locks_total. r012 tested the opposite extreme (2/-2) and was refuted, indicating the response is non-monotonic. Setting page=1 and relation=1 keeps promotion near the coarse end but avoids the degenerate zero-cap path, testing a distinct interior point on the same granularity axis with a new scalar prediction on locks_total.p95.

With page cap 0 and relation cap 0, every predicate lock is promoted immediately to the coarsest granularity, so each GetUserTweets scan performs maximal promotion bookkeeping and holds coarse relation-level SIRead locks that inflate locks_total and lengthen the p99 tail. Restoring PostgreSQL defaults (page=2, relation=-2, i.e. relation cap derived as a fraction of the per-txn budget) keeps locks at page granularity longer, cutting promotion churn and coarse-lock footprint. The r012 test of the same default pair was refuted only while the WAL commit-path bundle was simultaneously perturbed; with the accepted WAL bundle now fixed, this isolates the SIRead granularity axis.
